editorial.headline: The Business of Staging Sport
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a PMA registration at a Bali address is blocked by the province-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
93191 is the operational code for bringing a live sporting event into being. Its scope reaches from technical planning and provision through to the arrangement and operation of audiovisual equipment and special effects. It applies to sports weeks and other multi-event programmes as well as single-event championships. It also includes sports promotion services confined to sport, including esports promotion. In practical terms, this is the activity of managing, organising and running the presentation machinery of sport—not merely appearing within the event.

The code is open across the full stated business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the activity can sit with a small organiser as readily as with a larger operator handling technical delivery, event management or specialist promotion. Its PMA status is TERBUKA nationally, and its foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. The national position is therefore unambiguous: foreign investment may hold the full permitted stake under the cited PMA basis.

Bali changes the registration outcome. A foreign investor cannot register this activity at a Bali address today. The record identifies the Besar scale as Menengah Rendah and says that it is blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium. That moratorium applies island-wide and permanently to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The cited governor’s letter is dated May 2026; the record’s later note is dated June 2026. Neither the national openness nor the 100% national ceiling removes that Bali-address restriction.

For founders, this is a case where the activity description and the investment geography must be read together. The national framework permits full foreign ownership for the listed sports-event and sports-promotion work. Yet the Bali rule is decisive for a PMA registration located in the province: the activity is blocked there under the stated moratorium. The honest reading is not that foreign ownership is conditionally reduced in Bali, but that PMA registration at a Bali address is unavailable for this activity under the recorded rule.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this activity is nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration at a Bali address.
